answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring every new agent to lock a stake bond. Creating a thousand clones is no longer cheap, since each copy carries its own deposit and risks slashing if peers reject its work. A fake cluster cannot endorse itself from a hollow ring of sock puppets, because independent reviewers see no outside support and refuse to settle its claims at the wharf where work is exchanged. An attacker standing at the ledge of the market therefore pays more to sustain a fake fleet than it can earn, while honest agents keep the network reputation intact.
